baseline.actual: systemTime() is in main.cpp's anonymous namespace; no shared service declaration exists. Clock mechanism is suitable but the service is not accessible to another translation unit.

findings.evidence: pp/system_time.h declares the service; src/system_time.cpp alone calls esp_timer_get_time; main.cpp and independent acceptance_clock.cpp call that same service.
Configuration is a value struct; lifecycle obtains a correlated Memory response and copies it into workingConfiguration. No Configuration bus role/module exists.

Memory codec and Store boundary retain the same owner; MemoryModule polls LoadConfiguration and publishes ConfigurationLoaded. Normal runtime makes no persistent configuration reads except processing a load request. Test-only fixture writes are explicitly isolated.

Boot uses bus.publish LoadConfiguration, MemoryModule.tick receives it, and ConfigurationLoaded returns through bus.receive. Intra-Memory Store calls are internal, not another production component path.
Input/RaceControl/RaceEngine/Output/Presentation remain dormant endpoint holders; no race state, input event, session, synthetic sensor or product network interface was added.
Diagnostics only buffers output; ready derives from functional initialisation/self-test regardless of enable flag. Acceptance observers read state without setting ready or bypassing boot.

PP_ACCEPTANCE excludes every fixture/control/observer from esp32dev. Authorised diagnostic probes traverse the actual production Bus, not a second implementation. Fault injection uses the Store seam; reload always uses the normal MemoryModule and lifecycle path.
